claims.summary: The exported greatest-common-divisor function always returns the greatest common divisor of its two inputs treated as unsigned 32-bit numbers.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: For every pair of unsigned 32-bit inputs, the result is their greatest common divisor, including gcd(a, 0) = a. The examples agree with that guarantee.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: The claim covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, interpreted as unsigned natural numbers for the greatest-common-divisor calculation.
The result is converted to 32 bits; conversion wraps modulo 2 to the 32nd power, though this greatest common divisor already fits in 32 bits.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates, does not trap or throw, and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The result is the greatest common divisor of the two unsigned bit-vector values, not of signed interpretations of the inputs.

claims.summary: The exported clamp function returns the input limited by signed comparisons to the supplied bounds, using the claim’s lower-then-upper selection rule.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The statement uses signed comparisons and selects the lower bound first, then the upper bound, otherwise the input, matching the stated clamp rule. For example, with reversed bounds, clamp(3, 8, 2) returns 8 because the lower-bound condition is checked first.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: The claim covers every triple of 32-bit inputs.
Comparisons use signed 32-bit interpretation. The result is the lower bound when the input is below it, otherwise the upper bound when the input exceeds it, otherwise the input itself.
No arithmetic is performed, so there is no arithmetic wraparound; the result is one of the input bit patterns.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates, does not trap or throw, and returns exactly the selected value.
caveats: The claim does not require the lower bound to be less than or equal to the upper bound; it guarantees the stated selection even when the bounds are reversed.
The source notation’s conditional comparisons elaborate as comparisons explicitly tested equal to true; this is equivalent to the ordinary Boolean condition.
